newsitem.title: USA: Harnischfeger not seeking end of Giddings review.
newsitem.headline: Harnischfeger not seeking end of Giddings review.

text.p: Harnischfeger Industries Inc said Tuesday it was not demanding that Giddings & Lewis Inc, which it seeks to acquire in a hostile bid, terminate its review of strategic alternatives.

"You have stated that we 'demanded' you terminate your 'review of strategic alternatives,'" Jeffery Grade, Harnischfeger chairman, said in a statement that included a letter sent to Giddings & Lewis Chairman Marvin Isles.
On April 25, Harnischfeger announced a $19 a share offer for Giddings, a deal valued at about $747 million including the assumption of Giddings' debt. Giddings rejected that bid.

In a letter to Grade that Giddings released on Monday, Isles said, "We do not believe it is in our stockholders' best interests to provide Harnischfeger information merely to better enable it to pursue an offer that we find inadequate. Nor do we think our stockholders would be well served by our giving in to demands that we immediately terminate our reiew of strategic alternatives and allow you to proceed with your inadequate offer."
Giddings on Monday also stuck by its insistance that Harnischfeger agree not to pursue an unsolicited bid for two years before it reveals to Harnischfeger confidential financial information.

"Frankly, I cannot understand how providing Harnischfeger Industries, the only single party to make a firm public offer, the requested information is anything but beneficial to all G&L stockholders," Grade said in his letter.
Grade said Gidding & Lewis has been reviewing alternatives with advisors since March 7. "When may the stockholders of G&L know the outcome of these deliberations?" he added.
